recentItems.title: Why great art requires risk | Alex Van Halen, David Lee Roth & Robert Vargas | TEDxFargo
recentItems.description:
Art and music are extensions of who we are as human beings. 

Join Alex Van Halen + David Lee Roth, members of the legendary rock band Van Halen, and world renowned muralist Robert Vargas as they they examine how stepping outside of comfort zones, absorbing foreign cultures, and embracing contrasting creative approaches can enrich your work. Discover how keeping an audience within arm's reach allows creators to build genuine community through their craft. Alex Van Halen helped redefine the sound and spirit of rock & roll. Born in Amsterdam in 1953, he moved with his family to Pasadena, California, in 1962, where he and his younger brother, Eddie, began their lifelong creative partnership. Originally trained in classical piano and guitar, Alex found his voice behind the drums. In 1972, the brothers co-founded Van Halen, launching a band that would become one of rock's most influential acts. With his thunderous playing, signature double-bass technique, and massive custom drum kits, Alex powered iconic songs including “Hot for Teacher,” “Jump,” and “Runnin’ with the Devil.” Alongside Eddie, he was the only constant member throughout the band’s four-decade run. In 2024, he published Brothers, a deeply personal memoir celebrating family, music, loss, and the extraordinary partnership he shared with Eddie.

Robert Vargas has transformed walls around the world into larger-than-life works of art. Born and raised in Boyle Heights, Los Angeles, Vargas is an internationally renowned contemporary artist + muralist. Educated at the Los Angeles County High School for the Arts and Pratt Institute in Brooklyn, he is known for creating massive public murals entirely freehand, without grids, projections, or stencils. His high-profile works include Angelus, a 14-story mural in Downtown Los Angeles, and LA Rising, a 150-foot portrait of Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani. In 2021, Vargas created Long Live the King, a 17-foot mural honoring Eddie Van Halen on the exterior of Guitar Center’s flagship Hollywood store on the Sunset Strip, connecting his artistry to one of rock’s most legendary figures.

David Lee Roth solidified his legacy as one of rock’s most influential frontmen by channeling pure, sharp-witted charisma and an athletic stage presence. While attending Pasadena City College in Southern California, he met brothers Alex and Eddie Van Halen and became the lead vocalist of Van Halen in 1974. Roth's trademark acrobatic high kicks and electrifying energy helped propel the band to international superstardom, a run that peaked with their landmark album, 1984. Driven by the chart-topping smash hit “Jump," the RIAA Diamond-certified masterpiece became a cultural phenomenon. Roth then launched a highly successful solo career in 1985, scoring major hits with iconic covers of "California Girls" and "Just a Gigolo." A 2007 Van Halen reunion sparked massive worldwide arena tours—a triumphant return that culminated in the band’s induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame—permanently cementing David Lee Roth's legendary status. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: How I Failed as a Musician - So I Could Become an Artist | David Snyder | TEDxFargo
recentItems.description:
Speaker and composer David Snyder, based in Los Angeles, CA, shares the deeply personal story of how nine years of rigorous classical piano training shaped — and nearly broke — his identity as an artist. 

Through live music and original composition, the talk explores how discipline and rules aren't the enemy of creativity, but the foundation of it. Drawing from his own journey of quitting the piano after a devastating competition loss, moving to LA, and eventually becoming a professional musician and composer, the talk makes the case that you have to learn the rules before you can truly break them. Woven throughout with live piano performance — including an original composition written for his wife — the talk ultimately reveals what so many artists discover: that music can say the things we don't have the words for, and that our greatest creative breakthroughs often come from the very experiences that first seemed to destroy us. 
To learn more about David Snyder and his work, visit thepianosaysitbetter.com David Snyder is a pianist and composer redefining what the piano can be—turning it into a cinematic, electrifying storytelling experience. Blending virtuosic playing with bold improvisation and humor, his music moves from intimate emotion to explosive intensity, capturing audiences in seconds.

From sold-out performances across the country to viral videos seen by millions, he has built a reputation for making the piano feel fresh, unpredictable, and alive. As the creator of the one-man piano show, "The Piano Says It Better," he crafts immersive, story-driven shows that inspire audiences to rediscover creativity and find their own musical voice.

His mission: to prove that music isn’t just something you play—it’s something that can change your life. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: What if movie science could exist? | Sara Davis | TEDxFrancis Holland School Sloane Square
recentItems.description: Have you ever watched a science-fiction movie and wondered just how much of it could actually be possible? Have you ever seen a cool invention on screen and wondered if someone had managed to make something similar in reality? This talk aims to explore to what extent some of the core aspects of science-fiction movies could be re-created in real life, including AI and robots, aliens and space travel, and biologically enhanced and mutated beings. Sara Davis is a student in the Lower Sixth studying Mathematics, Chemistry and French. She hopes to study Chemistry or Linguistics at university, and is particularly interested in real world applications and possibilities. recentItems.title: What if we could know our future health? | Maia Redbourn | TEDxFrancis Holland School Sloane Square
recentItems.description: What if knowing your future health could help science find a cure but change how you live your life today? This talk explores the ethical and emotional weight behind knowing your future and how it may negatively impact people. On the converse this talk also discusses how knowing our future in terms of health would be incredibly beneficial for medicine and finding cures for diseases. Maia Redbourn is a student in the Lower Sixth studying Biology, Chemistry, Maths and Further Maths. She hopes to study Medicine at university, with a particular interest in Neurology. recentItems.title: Off The Timeline | Vineet Nambiar | TEDxYouth@MESIndianSchool
recentItems.description: Tech entrepreneur and global strategist Vineet Nambiar explores why expanding beyond traditional boundaries is no longer a luxury, but a necessity for long-term survival in an interconnected world. Drawing from nearly two decades of scaling ventures globally, he reveals how purpose-driven expansion, strategic adaptation, and cross-border collaboration enable organizations to build resilient solutions that thrive on the world stage. Vineet Nambiar is an entrepreneur, international director, and founder with nearly two decades of experience scaling ventures across global markets. Born and raised in Doha, Qatar, Vineet serves as the International Director of International Business Week and Chairman for Qatar at the Hong Kong–Middle East Business Chamber. The founder of Mavericks 365, an innovation and business acceleration platform, Vineet leverages his background in computer engineering and training from Carnegie Mellon University to help startups build resilience, expand internationally, and navigate cross-border trade. recentItems.title: I Grew a Mountain Forest Among Towers of Steel and Glass | WanPeng Zu | TEDxWukang Rd
recentItems.description:
As cities rise ever higher, why do people become increasingly disconnected from wind, trees, and the changing seasons? Landscape architect Wanpeng Zu begins with the concept of a "climbable mountain forest," bringing nature back into high-rise architecture. Through the exploration and everyday experiences of its users, the space gains an unexpected vitality. Sustainability is no longer just an idea on paper, but becomes part of daily life — transforming a space drawn by designers into a city truly lived by its people. 1、Global Urban Public Realm Explorer
2、Design Director at TLS | M.S. in Architecture and Urban Design, Columbia GSAPP

recentItems.title: 20 Years of Healing: The Rebirth of My Hometown Grassland | Trachung Palzang | TEDxWukang Rd
recentItems.description:
In ecological restoration on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau, high-tech solutions are not the only answer. Instead, Trachung Barang chose to return to the old ways—applying the time-honored, traditional knowledge passed down through generations of Tibetan herders to heal the land. Working with the rhythm of nature, he used the very hooves of livestock to trample seeds into the soil and their manure to nourish it, all while practicing scientific rotational grazing. This approach has successfully revived the once-desertifying grasslands, bringing them back to life.
His unwavering commitment embodies the true essence of sustainable development: respecting the land, revering nature, and trusting the pace of time. Like the resilient grass that anchors itself firmly in the earth, he guards the green of his homeland with a lifetime of patience. 1、20-Year Grassland Restoration Pioneer & Desertification Fighter
2、Recipients of “Rangeland Restoration Awards 2026”
3、The Subject of "Palzang the Herdsman" — A Gold Award-Winning Documentary at the UN Climate Conference
4、Founder of the Trachung Tsang Ecological and Cultural Development Center This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Invisible Vibration: Relearning How to Belong to the Earth | Alex Long Yuan | TEDxWukang Rd
recentItems.description:
The ecological crisis we face is, at its core, a crisis of perception. Through artificial intelligence, emotion technology, and interdisciplinary artistic practice, Alex Long Yuan transforms the subtle respiration of plants, the passage of time inscribed in tree rings, and fluctuations in human emotion into powerful experiences of light, sound, and space.
Inner sustainability forms a foundation for rebuilding our relationship with the world. True sustainability is not about humanity positioning itself above nature and attempting to “save” the Earth, but about rediscovering our resonance with the living world and relearning how to belong to this planet. 1、International Interdisciplinary Contemporary Artist
2、Emotion Tech Innovator. Co-founder of INOASIS
3、Sole Commissioned Artist for the UN Forest for Life Project This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Carbon Goals: A Distant Dream or the New Game Rules? | YingChu Qian | TEDxWukang Rd
recentItems.description:
When encountering grand concepts like "carbon neutrality" and "ESG" in the workplace, they often feel disconnected from our daily lives. Qian Yingchu breaks down the new rules of this era from a highly practical perspective. From the water-saving secrets of daily dishwashing to the massive value created by the meticulous management of commercial complexes, he demonstrates that carbon reduction is never an empty slogan or a cost burden, but a core competitive advantage for the future. Doing our everyday jobs to the highest standard is, in itself, the best form of carbon reduction. 1、Founder of HARVENCY Building Commissioning
2、Senior Advisor on Sino-US Clean Energy and Green Finance
